generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, the three moves run as one preparation for a single talk, whether it is a conference-style study presentation or a poster. You read the brief to see what the format rewards, build a structure and visual aids that fit it, then rehearse and check for the common errors before the day. Run as one practice, each move feeds the next, so the psychology you present lands as it should.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two psychology students prepare the same assessed presentation on a study. Tom works on each stage alone: slides first, the brief skimmed late, and no rehearsal. Amara runs the three moves as one practice, reading the brief, building a structure that fits, then rehearsing and trimming the slides for the common errors. Amara's talk fits the task and carries the group, because the moves worked together.
generatedProse.summary: Across your psychology presentations, these three moves are strongest run as one practice. Read the brief, build a fitting structure and visual aids, then rehearse and correct the common errors before the day. It is the practice, repeated, that makes your delivery reliable.

check.body: A student reads the brief for a poster, designs a clear visual layout to fit it, rehearses the two-minute summary to time, and trims a crowded panel before the day. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next report, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next report improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: The three moves working as one practice: adapting to the format, structuring and designing for it, and correcting the common errors.
_items.feedback: Yes. Reading the brief, designing to fit, and trimming for the errors are one connected run of preparation.
